mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: To test oil temperature, keep the oil temperature constant and change the dough thickness.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Changing oil temperature and dropping height together is a fair test if the dough thickness stays the same.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Since the difference is attributed to oil temperature, the dough thickness and dropping method must have been the same.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: A fair oil-temperature test must use the same oil temperature, dough thickness, and dropping method in both trials.

intelligence.enrichment: When comparing the effect of one factor, other relevant conditions should be kept the same; for oil temperature, use dough circles of the same thickness and drop them in the same way. Keeping other conditions the same makes the observed difference more attributable to the factor being tested. The learner plans a fair comparison by changing the tested factor and keeping relevant other conditions the same. Any two different puri trials make a fair comparison as long as puffing is observed.
